Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

text:
This looks like May 2010, the month of the flash crash and the European sovereign debt crisis.

- Unemployment at 9.9% fits spring 2010 (April was 9.9%, May 9.7%).
- The fed funds rate near 0.20% and a 10-year yield of 3.34% fit May 2010, when the 10-year fell from about 3.7% to 3.3%.
- US large-cap equity fell 9.5% in the month, in line with S&P 500's roughly -8% in May 2010, and the VIX near 29.7 fits too.
- Developed ex-US equity fell 12.3% in the month and gold rose 4%, consistent with the euro crisis.
- Core CPI at 0.98% YoY fits 2010.
- Industrial production at +5.18% YoY also fits 2010.
- Headline CPI at 2.24% YoY fits April 2010 (2.2%), and May was 2.0%. The data may be lagged by one month, which is consistent with May.

I settled on May 2010 rather than April because the equity drawdown and the 10-year yield level both point to the end of May.
